properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (fourth pass): a user-flagged visual check found this block's west edge still sitting on real pavement/curbside parking even after the transform and buffer fixes above. Root-caused: this part of the site (A/B/D/E1-E4 cluster, farthest from this transform's anchor points near Illinois/Michigan St) has a real residual scale/shear error -- confirmed by comparing the pixel gap between Blocks A and B (50px) against the real-world distance the transform produces for it (~17.6m, implying a ~2.84 px/m local scale) versus the transform's own Illinois-Michigan calibration (~3.4 px/m) -- a ~20% local discrepancy. Rather than keep tuning the transform, the west edge was instead measured directly against georeferenced ESRI World Imagery (the same satellite basemap used elsewhere in this project for visual validation): the real paved curb/parking-lot edge was located by eye against a fine lon/lat grid overlaid on the orthophoto, and this edge's coordinate was moved to match it, leaving the rest of the diagram-derived shape unchanged. This is a targeted, ground-truthed fix for this one edge, not a re-validated transform -- other edges of this block still come from the diagram transform and carry that same residual uncertainty. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): user-flagged visual check found this block's traced L-shape did not match Figure 6.4.2 at all -- overlaid directly on the source diagram, this file's shape cut through the '21' gray Historic Building box and extended into the open space south of it, nowhere near the real 90ft/65ft L-shaped fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated both this block's colors (90ft blue [128,193,219] and 65ft purple [169,143,173]) in a tight crop, merged them (closing the thin internal divider line between the two height zones), and extracted the true outer contour (OpenCV) -- a clean L-shape with the 90ft portion as a tall leg on the west side and the 65ft portion as a shorter extension to the east, both anchored at the same north edge, with the '21' gray box and surrounding white gap naturally excluded (they don't touch this color mask). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. New shape's total area (~1727 m2) is almost identical to the old, wrong shape's area (~1721 m2) -- the previous trace was misshapen, not mis-scaled. This resolves BOTH of this file's previously-documented overlaps with Building 21 (429.8 m2) and Elevation Sky Park (217.6 m2) down to zero -- those overlaps were an artifact of E1's own bad shape, not of Building 21 or ESP's placement (see those files' own notes, corrected accordingly). CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (street/curb re-anchoring pass, prompted by a user question about validation process consistency): this block's own north edge was directly confirmed, by rendering it against Esri World Imagery, to sit on top of real, currently-paved, actively-used street pavement (visible lane markings and/or vehicles in the satellite image), not a corner-lot sliver -- one of several Pier 70 blocks found this way after this project switched its real-street reference from OSM (community-traced, name-matched ways) to DataSF's own official Street Centerline / Curbs and Islands datasets (src/street_geometry.py), which for the first time gave an accurate enough curb position to see it. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer (6.8m centerline half-width, empirically measured against real curb data near Pier 70 -- see street_geometry.py); area 1733 -> 677 sq m. The clip's result was a MultiPolygon (the street cut disconnected a 102 sq m sliver from the main body); kept only the larger piece, consistent with how this project has handled the same situation elsewhere (Mission Rock Square, Potrero Block 7). This is a targeted correction of this block's street-facing edge, not a re-verified re-trace of its other edges, which still carry this site's usual diagram-transform uncertainty. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the DataSF identifiers named above (Building 14's footprint under blklot 4052001; Building 12's Assessor parcel blklot 4114010) are our own lookups in DataSF's Building Footprints and Assessor parcels layers, not statements in the D4D, which this file cites only for the diagram. Assessor lot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF acdm-wktn) and its legacy id is carried by 21 building footprints, so the id does not by itself identify Building 14; 4114010 is an active P70-MU lot at 1070 Maryland St that DataSF does not name as Building 12. Nothing in the geometry was changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data -- see digitization_method.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this file uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat. Status 'planned' as of Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026), which says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward.'.

Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. properties.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential, mostly 90 ft max with a smaller 65 ft strip along its north leg per Figure 6.4.2. No construction-start source found. Geometry here is a simplified bounding shape -- the real parcel has an irregular footprint around the historic Building 21 (mapped separately in this project) immediately to its southeast.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see the accuracy note. Status 'planned' as of Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026), which says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward.
